title: The Next Opener: What Profile Should Mumbai Indians Scout?
dek: What should Mumbai Indians look for in their next opener? The current IPL market sets the bar: how fast the best openers score and how long they survive.
excerpt: Since 2024, no IPL opener has combined a top-quarter strike rate with above-median survival. Mumbai Indians have to choose which of the two to prioritise.

sections.heading: Where the Bar Is Now
body: Opening in the IPL has changed: the powerplay is now attacked from the first ball. A scout needs to know both how fast the best openers score and how long they last.
Since 2024, the top quarter of IPL openers by strike rate scored at {{ev:no-q75}} or faster, and the median opener lasted {{ev:no-bpdmed}} balls per dismissal (min. one hundred and fifty balls).

sections.heading: The Profile to Scout
body: No opener met both standards, which shows how rarely tempo and survival come together. The chart lists the fastest qualifying openers instead.
A scout should look for players already close to both lines, not just the fastest scorers.

sections.heading: Speed Versus Survival
body: Strike rate and survival trade off: the fastest openers often get out sooner. The right balance depends on the batting depth behind them.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Fast and Durable, or Fast With Depth Behind
body: Mumbai Indians should scout openers who meet both standards, or accept a faster but less durable opener only if the middle order is deep enough to absorb early wickets.
The batting-depth articles in this series measure that cushion.
